chunks: Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub and Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, concerning:

A man who accuses another man falsely, then is flogged, then returns to accuse him again—he said: “If he says to him, ‘What I said to you is true,’ he is not to be flogged. But if he accuses him of zina after he has already been flogged, then the hadd is upon him. And if he accuses him before he is flogged with ten accusations, then there is only one hadd upon him.”

key_terms.فَيُجْلَدُ: then he is flogged as the prescribed punishment
key_terms.يَقْذِفُ: to accuse someone of illicit sexual conduct

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone repeats an accusation of zina after already receiving the hadd for qadhf?
ai.summary: This hadith explains legal rulings concerning repeated qadhf accusations and when the hadd punishment is reapplied. It distinguishes between reaffirming a previous statement, making a fresh accusation after punishment, and repeating multiple accusations before the hadd is carried out.
